query: Help me understand the key points in this table — what should I concentrate on?

per_column.name: Sentiment
per_column.rationale: Overall positive/negative sentiment is a holistic summary of the review's evaluation, i.e. a restatement of the whole quality judgment rather than a specific aspect OF service quality.

per_column.name: Issues_Flagged
per_column.rationale: A multi-label list (seat; delay; food; staff; entertainment) bundles several aspects into one column. It re-aggregates facets rather than isolating a single non-overlapping aspect, so it duplicates the aspects captured by dedicated facet columns.

per_column.name: Key_Focus_Point
per_column.rationale: This picks which single aspect dominates a review; it is a meta-selector over facets, not itself an aspect OF service quality, and its values overlap with the underlying facets.

per_column.name: Needs_Attention
per_column.rationale: A downstream action flag (Yes/No) derived from quality; it is a consequence/decision about quality, not a constitutive part of it.

per_column.name: Review_Length
per_column.rationale: A mechanical text metric of the review string; it says nothing about any aspect of the airline's service quality.

judge.rationale: None of the added columns are constitutive facets (parts) of airline_service_quality. Genuine facets already exist in the original table (Seat Comfort, Staff Service, Food & Beverages, Inflight Entertainment, Value For Money), but the augmentation added holistic restatements (Sentiment, Key_Focus_Point, Issues_Flagged), a downstream decision flag (Needs_Attention), and a mechanical text metric (Review_Length). Issues_Flagged, Key_Focus_Point and Sentiment substantially overlap in the aspects they reference, hurting mutual exclusivity, and no set of clean part-of aspects is introduced, so exhaustiveness against the concept is very low.
